newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MPs push for arms deals by public tender.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MPs push for arms deals by public tender.

text.p: Five Kuwaiti parliamentarians have presented a bill for the purchase of all military hardware by public tender to cut costs, an MP said on Sunday.
"We presented the bill which is aimed at controlling expenditure and removing military (procurement) officials from the circle of doubts," Nasser al-Sanea told Reuters.
Kuwait, among the world's leading arms importers, launched a $12 billion plan to 2004 to rearm its military after the 1991 Gulf War freed it from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
The bill calls for the formation of a specialised committee to finalise arms purchases by the military and another for requirements by the National Guard and Interior Ministry.
Parliamentarians often criticise large commissions for brokers in arms deals and the last parliament, which ended its term in October, had opened several inquiries into alleged irregularities.
Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said in December that Kuwait had eliminated middlemen from weapons purchases to cut costs.
